subject: English
passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Florence Price was a pioneering composer.
• Her first published musical composition was a symphony.
• It was called "Symphony in E Minor."
• It first appeared in Musical Quarterly in 1932.
prompt: The student wants to identify the title of Florence Price's first published symphony. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Florence Price's first published musical composition appeared in 1932.
choices.B: Pioneering composer Florence Price's first published musical composition was a symphony.
choices.C: In 1932, a symphony by Florence Price appeared in Musical Quarterly.
choices.D: Florence Price's first published symphony was called "Symphony in E Minor."

explanation: Choice D is the best answer because it directly accomplishes the stated goal of identifying the title of Florence Price's first published symphony. By explicitly stating that the work "was called 'Symphony in E Minor,'" this choice synthesizes the essential information from notes 2 and 3 to provide the specific title the student wants to identify. The sentence focuses precisely on what the goal requires: naming the work rather than providing surrounding contextual details about when or where it was published.
